Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 103, verse 1:

(p-197) Surat al-'Asr

Meccan, and its number of verses is three.

﴿By the afternoon.﴾ Glorified is He, Who swears by the afternoon prayer (ṣalāt al-'aṣr) because of its outstanding excellence; or by the evening (al-'ashiyy), which is the period between the decline of the sun (al-zawāl) and sunset (al-ghurūb), just as He swears by the forenoon (al-ḍuḥā); or by the age of Prophethood (ʿaṣr al-nubuwwa), because of the manifest excellence of that age over all other ages; or by time (al-dahr), because it encompasses the wondrous affairs, both those that remain and those that pass away.

Indeed, mankind is in loss. ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ means: in loss in their trade and their endeavors, and in spending their lives on their aims. The definite article in al-insan is for the genus (the whole of mankind), and the indefinite noun khusr is for magnification (an extraordinary and immense loss).

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 103, verse 3:

﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, for they are in a commerce that will never perish, as they have sold the transient and base for the lasting and precious, and have exchanged the lasting righteous deeds (al-baqiyat al-salihat) for the fleeting morning and evening things (al-ghadiyat al-ra'ihat). How excellent a bargain it is, how profitable! This is an explanation of their perfecting themselves. His Exalted saying, ﴿and they enjoined one another to the truth﴾ and so on, is an explanation of their perfecting others, that is: some of them enjoined others to the established matter that cannot be denied, and whose good effects do not cease in either abode, and that is all good: belief in God, Mighty and Majestic, and following His books and messengers in every creed and action. ﴿And they enjoined one another to patience﴾, that is: patience regarding the sins to which the soul yearns by the judgment of human natural disposition (al-jibillah al-bashariyyah), and patience in the acts of obedience that are hard to perform, or in what God, Mighty and Majestic, tests His servants with. The specific mention of this mutual enjoining, although it falls under enjoining one another to the truth, is to display complete concern for it, or because the first refers to the rank of worship ('ibadah), which is doing what God, Exalted, is pleased with, and the second refers to the rank of servitude ('ubudiyyah), which is contentment with what God, Exalted, has done. The meaning of patience is not merely restraining the soul from what it longs for, whether doing or abstaining; rather, it is receiving what comes from Him, Exalted, with graciousness and contentment with it outwardly and inwardly.

From the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surah al-'Asr, God, Exalted, will forgive him, and he will be among those who enjoined one another to the truth and enjoined one another to patience."
